61	 * than this, no matter how many newer builds have buried it. This is what

95	 * honestly: a MANUAL resend from the Stripe dashboard of an event older than a

97	 * otherwise grows forever, and the mitigation is human: a year-old manual
98	 * resend should be checked by hand anyway.
99	 */
100	export const STRIPE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365;

102	/**
103	 * Rows touched per statement. Deliberately modest: this job runs against the
104	 * live database while people are using the product, and the point of batching
105	 * is that no single statement holds locks long enough to be noticed. A bigger
106	 * batch would finish sooner and serve users worse.
107	 */
108	export const BATCH_SIZE = 500;

110	/**
111	 * Hard stop on the batch loop. Every loop below terminates on its own because
112	 * each pass narrows the candidate set, but "should terminate" is not a
113	 * property worth betting a production table on. If a delete ever silently
114	 * affects zero rows, this is what stops the script instead of spinning.
115	 */
116	const MAX_BATCHES = 20_000;

118	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
119	// Types
120	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
121	
122	/** What a rule would remove. Produced by SELECTs only. */
123	export type RetentionCount = {
124	  /** Rows the rule would delete (or, for snapshots, blank out). */
125	  rows: number;
126	  /** Rows currently in the target table, for context. */
127	  total: number;
128	  /**
129	   * Estimated bytes reclaimed, or null when it cannot be estimated. Postgres
130	   * returns freed space to the table's own free list, not to the filesystem,
131	   * until the table is vacuumed — see docs/retention.md.
132	   */
133	  bytes: number | null;
134	};
135	
136	/** What a rule actually removed. */
137	export type RetentionPurge = {
138	  rows: number;
139	  batches: number;
140	  /** True if MAX_BATCHES stopped the loop early — re-run to finish. */
141	  truncated: boolean;
142	};

144	export type RetentionRule = {
145	  /** Stable key, also what `--only` matches. */
146	  key: string;
147	  title: string;
148	  /** Table (and column, when the rule blanks a column rather than deleting). */
149	  target: string;
150	  /** Human-readable threshold, printed by the runner and quoted in the docs. */
151	  threshold: string;
152	  /** One-line justification, printed by the runner. */
153	  rationale: string;
154	  /** SELECT-only. Never mutates. */
155	  count: () => Promise<RetentionCount>;
156	  /** Mutates. Only ever reached via an explicit --apply. */
157	  purge: () => Promise<RetentionPurge>;

164	export function daysAgo(days: number): Date {
165	  return new Date(Date.now() - days * 86_400_000);
166	}

168	/**
169	 * Total on-disk size of a table including its indexes and TOAST. Used to turn
170	 * a row count into a byte estimate proportionally, which is cheap and — unlike
171	 * summing row widths — accounts for the index entries that also go away.
172	 */
173	async function relationBytes(table: string): Promise<number | null> {
174	  const rows = await db.$queryRaw<{ size: bigint | null }[]>`
175	    SELECT pg_total_relation_size(${`"${table}"`}::regclass) AS size`;
176	  const size = rows[0]?.size;
177	  return size == null ? null : Number(size);
178	}
179	
180	/** Proportional byte estimate: whole-table size scaled by the share going away. */
181	async function estimateBytes(table: string, rows: number, total: number): Promise<number | null> {
182	  if (rows === 0) return 0;
183	  if (total === 0) return null;
184	  const size = await relationBytes(table);
185	  return size === null ? null : Math.round((size * rows) / total);
186	}

188	/**
189	 * The one batched-mutation loop, shared by every rule.
190	 *
191	 * `selectIds` hands back at most `take` ids that still match the rule, and
192	 * `mutate` removes them. Each pass re-runs the selection rather than paging
193	 * with an offset, so rows the previous pass handled drop out of the candidate
194	 * set naturally and concurrent inserts cannot shift a window underneath us.
195	 */
196	async function purgeInBatches(
197	  selectIds: (take: number) => Promise<string[]>,
198	  mutate: (ids: string[]) => Promise<number>,
199	): Promise<RetentionPurge> {
200	  let rows = 0;
201	  let batches = 0;
202	
203	  while (batches < MAX_BATCHES) {
204	    const ids = await selectIds(BATCH_SIZE);
205	    if (ids.length === 0) return { rows, batches, truncated: false };
206	
207	    const affected = await mutate(ids);
208	    batches++;
209	    rows += affected;
210	
211	    // Selected rows but changed none: the mutation is not narrowing the
212	    // candidate set, so the next pass would select the same ids forever.
213	    if (affected === 0) return { rows, batches, truncated: true };
214	  }
215	
216	  return { rows, batches, truncated: true };
217	}

219	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
220	// Rule: expired sessions
221	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
222	
223	function sessionCutoff(): Date {
224	  return daysAgo(SESSION_GRACE_DAYS);
225	}
226	
227	export async function countExpiredSessions(): Promise<RetentionCount> {
228	  const where = { expiresAt: { lt: sessionCutoff() } };
229	  const [rows, total] = await Promise.all([db.session.count({ where }), db.session.count()]);
230	  return { rows, total, bytes: await estimateBytes("Session", rows, total) };
231	}
232	
233	export async function purgeExpiredSessions(): Promise<RetentionPurge> {
234	  const cutoff = sessionCutoff();
235	  return purgeInBatches(
236	    async (take) => {
237	      const rows = await db.session.findMany({
238	        where: { expiresAt: { lt: cutoff } },
239	        select: { id: true },
240	        orderBy: { expiresAt: "asc" },
241	        take,
242	      });
243	      return rows.map((r) => r.id);
244	    },
245	    async (ids) => (await db.session.deleteMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })).count,
246	  );
247	}

249	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
250	// Rule: stale build snapshots
251	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
252	
253	// Rank successful builds newest-first WITHIN each project, then take the ones
254	// that are both buried past SNAPSHOT_KEEP_PER_PROJECT and older than
255	// SNAPSHOT_MIN_AGE_DAYS, and that still carry a snapshot.
256	//
257	// The ranking runs over all SUCCEEDED builds, not only the ones that still
258	// have a snapshot, so "the 20 newest checkpoints" means the same thing on the
259	// second run as on the first — already-cleared builds keep their rank instead
260	// of letting the window creep forward run after run.
261	//
262	// Note this deliberately ignores FAILED builds: they never get a snapshot in
263	// the first place (app/api/generate/route.ts only writes one on success).
264	const staleSnapshotSource = (cutoff: Date) => Prisma.sql`
265	  FROM (
266	    SELECT b.id,
267	           b."filesSnapshot" AS snapshot,
268	           b."createdAt"     AS created_at,
269	           row_number() OVER (
270	             PARTITION BY b."projectId"
271	             ORDER BY b."createdAt" DESC, b.id DESC
272	           ) AS rn
273	    FROM "Build" b
274	    WHERE b.status = 'SUCCEEDED'
275	  ) ranked
276	  WHERE ranked.rn > ${SNAPSHOT_KEEP_PER_PROJECT}
277	    AND ranked.created_at < ${cutoff}
278	    AND ranked.snapshot IS NOT NULL`;

280	export async function countStaleBuildSnapshots(): Promise<RetentionCount> {
281	  const cutoff = daysAgo(SNAPSHOT_MIN_AGE_DAYS);
282	
283	  // pg_column_size reports the stored (TOAST-compressed) width, which is the
284	  // honest number here — it is what the snapshot actually costs on disk, not
285	  // what the JSON would measure if you printed it.
286	  const [row] = await db.$queryRaw<{ rows: number; bytes: bigint }[]>`
287	    SELECT count(*)::int AS rows,
288	           COALESCE(SUM(pg_column_size(ranked.snapshot)), 0)::bigint AS bytes
289	    ${staleSnapshotSource(cutoff)}`;
290	
291	  const total = await db.build.count({ where: { filesSnapshot: { not: Prisma.DbNull } } });
292	
293	  return { rows: row?.rows ?? 0, total, bytes: Number(row?.bytes ?? 0) };
294	}

296	export async function purgeStaleBuildSnapshots(): Promise<RetentionPurge> {
297	  const cutoff = daysAgo(SNAPSHOT_MIN_AGE_DAYS);
298	
299	  return purgeInBatches(
300	    async (take) => {
301	      const rows = await db.$queryRaw<{ id: string }[]>`
302	        SELECT ranked.id
303	        ${staleSnapshotSource(cutoff)}
304	        ORDER BY ranked.created_at ASC
305	        LIMIT ${take}`;
306	      return rows.map((r) => r.id);
307	    },
308	    // The Build row itself stays — only the snapshot column is emptied. See
309	    // NEVER_PRUNED: deleting builds would break the lifetime cost aggregates
310	    // and detach the credit ledger.
311	    async (ids) =>
312	      (
313	        await db.build.updateMany({
314	          where: { id: { in: ids } },
315	          data: { filesSnapshot: Prisma.DbNull },
316	        })
317	      ).count,
318	  );
319	}

322	// Rule: old analytics events
323	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

332	  const cutoff = daysAgo(EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS);
333	  return purgeInBatches(
334	    async (take) => {
335	      const rows = await db.event.findMany({
336	        where: { createdAt: { lt: cutoff } },
337	        select: { id: true },
338	        orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" },
339	        take,
340	      });
341	      return rows.map((r) => r.id);
342	    },
343	    async (ids) => (await db.event.deleteMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })).count,
344	  );
345	}

348	// Rule: old Stripe idempotency records
349	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
350	
351	export async function countOldStripeEvents(): Promise<RetentionCount> {
352	  const where = { createdAt: { lt: daysAgo(STRIPE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS) } };
353	  const [rows, total] = await Promise.all([db.stripeEvent.count({ where }), db.stripeEvent.count()]);
354	  return { rows, total, bytes: await estimateBytes("StripeEvent", rows, total) };
355	}

358	  const cutoff = daysAgo(STRIPE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS);
359	  return purgeInBatches(
360	    async (take) => {
361	      const rows = await db.stripeEvent.findMany({
362	        where: { createdAt: { lt: cutoff } },
363	        select: { id: true },
364	        orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" },
365	        take,
366	      });

368	    },
369	    async (ids) => (await db.stripeEvent.deleteMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })).count,
370	  );
371	}

374	// The policy
375	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
376	
377	export const RETENTION_RULES: RetentionRule[] = [
378	  {
379	    key: "sessions",
380	    title: "Expired sign-in sessions",
381	    target: "Session",
382	    threshold: "expired (SESSION_DAYS = 30 in lib/auth.ts)",
383	    rationale: "Already invalid at read time; the row is liability with no function.",
384	    count: countExpiredSessions,
385	    purge: purgeExpiredSessions,
386	  },
387	  {
388	    key: "build-snapshots",
389	    title: "Stale rollback snapshots",
390	    target: "Build.filesSnapshot",
391	    threshold: `older than ${SNAPSHOT_MIN_AGE_DAYS}d AND past the newest ${SNAPSHOT_KEEP_PER_PROJECT} per project`,
392	    rationale: "Rollback reaches back a few edits, not a few hundred. Build rows are kept.",
393	    count: countStaleBuildSnapshots,
394	    purge: purgeStaleBuildSnapshots,
395	  },
396	  {
397	    key: "events",
398	    title: "Analytics events",
399	    target: "Event",
400	    threshold: `older than ${EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS}d (~13 months)`,
401	    rationale: "Every dashboard reads a 30-day window; 400d only preserves year-over-year.",
402	    count: countOldEvents,

412	    purge: purgeOldStripeEvents,

104	const INPUT_ELEMENT_RE = /<\s*(?:input|textarea)\b|["'`](?:input|textarea)["'`]\s*,/gi;
105	
106	// Deliberately NOT bare "sign in" / "log in": those are ordinary nav labels on
107	// legitimate SaaS and e-commerce sites and were the single largest source of
108	// false positives while tuning this. What distinguishes a phishing page is
109	// second-person *solicitation* — it asks you to hand something over, usually
110	// with manufactured urgency.
111	const CREDENTIAL_SOLICITATION_RE = new RegExp(
112	  [
113	    /(?:sign|log)\s?in(?:to|\s+to)\s+(?:your|the)\b/.source,
114	    /enter\s+your\s+(?:password|credentials|pin|passcode)/.source,
115	    /(?:verify|confirm|validate)\s+your\s+(?:account|identity|password|login|details)/.source,
116	    /your\s+account\s+(?:has\s+been|was|will\s+be)\s+(?:suspended|locked|limited|disabled|closed)/.source,
117	    /unusual\s+(?:sign[-\s]?in|login|activity)/.source,
118	    /re-?enter\s+your\s+password/.source,
119	    /(?:your\s+)?session\s+(?:has\s+)?expired/.source,
120	    /update\s+your\s+(?:billing|payment|account)\s+(?:info|information|details)/.source,
121	    /(?:account|password)\s+recovery\s+required/.source,
122	  ].join("|"),
123	  "gi",
124	);
125	
126	// A brand named in one of these positions is being credited, linked, or offered
127	// as an OAuth provider — not impersonated. "Sign in with Google" next to a
128	// password field is the most common LEGITIMATE login page on the internet and
129	// must never be treated as a Google clone.
130	const BENIGN_BRAND_CONTEXT_RE =
131	  /(?:with|via|using|through|powered\s+by|we\s+accept|accepts?|pay\s+(?:with|by)|follow\s+us\s+on|find\s+us\s+on|share\s+on|available\s+on|download\s+on|get\s+it\s+on|integrat\w*\s+with|connects?\s+(?:to|with)|sync\w*\s+with|import\s+from|works\s+with|listen\s+on|watch\s+on|streaming\s+on|now\s+on|(?:as\s+)?seen\s+on|up\s+on|order\s+(?:on|via)|alternative\s+to|switch\s+from|migrat\w*\s+from|unlike|better\s+than|instead\s+of|such\s+as|like)\s*$/i;
132	
133	// The most-phished consumer brands. Each pattern is deliberately TIGHTER than
134	// the bare brand name, because bare names collide with legitimate copy in ways
135	// that matter: "apple" is on a coffee shop's menu, "meta" is in every <meta>
136	// tag, "chase" and "wise" are ordinary English words, "steam" is what a milk
137	// frother does. Where a bare name is unambiguous enough to stand alone it is
138	// still only one leg of a three-part conjunction (see the rule below).
139	const IMPERSONATION_TARGETS: { brand: string; re: RegExp }[] = [
140	  { brand: "Microsoft", re: /\bmicrosoft\s+(?:account|365|office|sign[-\s]?in)\b|\boffice\s?365\b|\boutlook\.com\b/gi },
141	  { brand: "Google", re: /\bgoogle\s+account\b|\bgmail\s+(?:account|sign[-\s]?in|login|password)\b|\baccounts\.google\.com\b/gi },
142	  { brand: "Apple", re: /\bapple\s?id\b|\bicloud\b|\bapple\s+account\b/gi },
143	  { brand: "Amazon", re: /\bamazon\s+(?:account|sign[-\s]?in|login)\b/gi },
144	  { brand: "PayPal", re: /\bpaypal\b/gi },
145	  { brand: "Netflix", re: /\bnetflix\b/gi },
146	  { brand: "Facebook", re: /\bfacebook\b/gi },
147	  { brand: "Instagram", re: /\binstagram\b/gi },
148	  { brand: "LinkedIn", re: /\blinkedin\b/gi },
149	  { brand: "WhatsApp", re: /\bwhatsapp\b/gi },
150	  { brand: "Dropbox", re: /\bdropbox\b/gi },
151	  { brand: "Adobe", re: /\badobe\s+(?:id|account|sign[-\s]?in)\b/gi },
152	  { brand: "DocuSign", re: /\bdocusign\b/gi },
153	  { brand: "Coinbase", re: /\bcoinbase\b/gi },
154	  { brand: "Binance", re: /\bbinance\b/gi },
155	  { brand: "Kraken", re: /\bkraken\s+(?:account|exchange|sign[-\s]?in)\b/gi },
156	  { brand: "MetaMask", re: /\bmetamask\b/gi },
157	  { brand: "Trust Wallet", re: /\btrust\s?wallet\b/gi },
158	  { brand: "Ledger", re: /\bledger\s+(?:live|wallet|nano)\b/gi },
159	  { brand: "Trezor", re: /\btrezor\b/gi },
160	  { brand: "Phantom Wallet", re: /\bphantom\s+wallet\b/gi },
161	  { brand: "Chase", re: /\bchase\s+bank\b|\bchase\.com\b/gi },
162	  { brand: "Wells Fargo", re: /\bwells\s+fargo\b/gi },
163	  { brand: "Bank of America", re: /\bbank\s+of\s+america\b/gi },
164	  { brand: "Citibank", re: /\bciti(?:bank)?\s+(?:account|online|sign[-\s]?in)\b/gi },
165	  { brand: "HSBC", re: /\bhsbc\b/gi },
166	  { brand: "Barclays", re: /\bbarclays\b/gi },
167	  { brand: "Revolut", re: /\brevolut\b/gi },
168	  { brand: "Venmo", re: /\bvenmo\b/gi },
169	  { brand: "Cash App", re: /\bcash\s?app\b/gi },
170	  { brand: "Zelle", re: /\bzelle\b/gi },
171	  { brand: "DHL", re: /\bdhl\b/gi },
172	  { brand: "FedEx", re: /\bfedex\b/gi },
173	  { brand: "USPS", re: /\busps\b/gi },
174	  { brand: "IRS", re: /\birs\.gov\b|\binternal\s+revenue\s+service\b/gi },
175	  { brand: "HMRC", re: /\bhmrc\b/gi },
176	  { brand: "Steam", re: /\bsteam\s+(?:account|guard|community)\b|\bsteamcommunity\b/gi },
177	  { brand: "Roblox", re: /\broblox\b/gi },
178	  { brand: "Discord", re: /\bdiscord\b(?!(?:app)?\.com\/api\/webhooks)/gi },
179	  { brand: "TikTok", re: /\btiktok\b/gi },
180	  { brand: "Spotify", re: /\bspotify\b/gi },
181	];
182	
183	// Drop sites that ship inside off-the-shelf phishing kits. Every one of these
184	// only counts when the file also collects a password — the signal is a password
185	// going to a channel like this, not the channel existing.
186	//
187	// `nearPassword` splits them by how innocent the channel is on its own:
188	//   • false — a Telegram bot, a Discord webhook, or an off-origin .php collector
189	//     has no legitimate role anywhere in a generated static marketing site, so
190	//     anywhere in the same file is damning enough.
191	//   • true  — formsubmit.co and mailto: are the NORMAL way a static site wires
192	//     up a contact form. A site with a contact form in the footer and a members
193	//     login on another page would otherwise be blocked outright, which is
194	//     exactly the kind of false positive that makes a gate like this
195	//     unshippable. These have to be wired to the password form itself.
196	const EXFIL_CHANNELS: { name: string; re: RegExp; nearPassword: boolean }[] = [
197	  { name: "Telegram bot API", re: /api\.telegram\.org\/bot/gi, nearPassword: false },
198	  { name: "Discord webhook", re: /discord(?:app)?\.com\/api\/webhooks/gi, nearPassword: false },
199	  {
200	    name: "off-origin PHP collector",
201	    re: /(?:action\s*[:=]\s*|fetch\s*\(\s*|axios\.post\s*\(\s*|sendBeacon\s*\(\s*)["'`](?:https?:)?\/\/[^"'`\s]+\.php\b/gi,
202	    nearPassword: false,
203	  },
204	  { name: "formsubmit.co relay", re: /\bformsubmit\.co\b/gi, nearPassword: true },
205	  { name: "mailto: form action", re: /action\s*[:=]\s*["'`]mailto:[^"'`]{1,120}/gi, nearPassword: true },
206	];
207	
208	// How far a "normally innocent" exfil channel may sit from a password field and
209	// still be read as the destination for it. One <form> of markup, roughly.
210	const SAME_FORM_RADIUS = 900;
211	
212	const OFF_ORIGIN_POST_RE =
213	  /(?:action\s*[:=]\s*|fetch\s*\(\s*|axios\.post\s*\(\s*|navigator\.sendBeacon\s*\(\s*)["'`](https?:\/\/[^"'`\s]{4,160})/gi;
214	
215	const SEED_PHRASE_RE =
216	  /\b(?:seed\s+phrase|recovery\s+phrase|secret\s+recovery\s+phrase|mnemonic(?:\s+phrase)?|(?:12|18|24)[-\s]word\s+(?:phrase|seed)|wallet\s+private\s+key|keystore\s+(?:file|json))\b/gi;
217	
218	// Security-education copy ("never share your seed phrase with anyone") reads
219	// almost identically to a drainer's own form label. If the surrounding text is
220	// a warning, the finding is downgraded rather than dropped — still recorded.
221	const SEED_WARNING_RE = /\b(?:never|do\s*n[o']t|no\s+one|nobody|don't)\b[^.!?]{0,90}\b(?:share|enter|reveal|type|give|ask|store)\b/i;
222	
223	const WALLET_CONNECT_RE =
224	  /window\.ethereum|eth_requestAccounts|@?walletconnect|window\.solana|window\.phantom|web3modal|BrowserProvider|Web3Provider|rainbowkit/gi;
225	
226	// Asset-DELEGATION primitives, not payment primitives. A legitimate "donate
227	// ETH" button uses eth_sendTransaction with a fixed value — that is deliberately
228	// NOT in this list, because flagging it would punish an honest crypto site. What
229	// a drainer needs, and an honest site does not, is permission to move assets it
230	// does not own: an unlimited allowance, setApprovalForAll, or an offline Permit
231	// signature.
232	// A note on why the raw 4-byte selectors are here as well as the method names:
233	// the method name often does NOT survive the build. A drainer that hand-rolls
234	// its calldata leaves only `"0xa22cb465…"` in the minified bundle — verified
235	// against real `vite build` output, where a `/* setApprovalForAll */` comment
236	// next to that selector was stripped and the name-based pattern went silent.
237	// An 8-hex-digit selector literal is an exact string with no plausible
238	// accidental collision, and it is still only one leg of the conjunction.
239	const DRAINER_PRIMITIVES: { name: string; re: RegExp }[] = [
240	  { name: "setApprovalForAll", re: /\bsetApprovalForAll\b|0xa22cb465/g },
241	  { name: "increaseAllowance", re: /\bincreaseAllowance\b|0x39509351/g },
242	  { name: "unlimited ERC-20 allowance", re: /[fF]{60,}|\bMaxUint256\b|\bMAX_UINT256\b|2\s*\*\*\s*256/g },
243	  { name: "off-chain Permit signature", re: /eth_signTypedData(?:_v[34])?|\bsignTypedData\b/g },
244	  { name: "delegated transferFrom", re: /\btransferFrom\s*\(|0x23b872dd|0x42842e0e|0xf242432a|0x2eb2c2d6/g },
245	];
246	
247	// eval-of-decoded-string. Minifiers produce dense code but never this shape;
248	// phishing kits and drainer templates ship it routinely to hide the drop URL.
249	const OBFUSCATED_PAYLOAD_RE =
250	  /\beval\s*\(\s*(?:atob|unescape|decodeURIComponent|String\.fromCharCode)|\bnew\s+Function\s*\(\s*(?:atob|unescape)|document\.write\s*\(\s*(?:unescape|atob)/gi;
251	
252	// ── Engine ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
253	
254	const EVIDENCE_RADIUS = 60;
255	// Tuned against real `vite build` output, not guessed. Phishing copy names the
256	// brand INSIDE the solicitation ("Sign in to your Microsoft account", "Your
257	// PayPal account has been limited"), so the two land within a few dozen
258	// characters of each other once class attributes are stripped. A legitimate
259	// page that happens to contain both — a film blog with a member login in one
260	// section and "now streaming on Netflix" in another — keeps them hundreds of
261	// characters apart. 120 sits in that gap with room on both sides.
262	const BRAND_WINDOW_RADIUS = 120;
263	// Wider, because a label and its <input> can legitimately be separated by a
264	// wrapper element or two.
265	const INPUT_WINDOW_RADIUS = 220;
266	const MAX_FINDINGS_PER_RULE = 3;
267	
268	function snippet(content: string, index: number, length: number): string {
269	  const start = Math.max(0, index - EVIDENCE_RADIUS);
270	  const end = Math.min(content.length, index + length + EVIDENCE_RADIUS);
271	  const raw = content.slice(start, end).replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
272	  return (start > 0 ? "…" : "") + raw + (end < content.length ? "…" : "");
273	}
274	
275	function windowAround(content: string, index: number, length: number, radius: number): string {
276	  return content.slice(
277	    Math.max(0, index - radius),
278	    Math.min(content.length, index + length + radius),
279	  );
280	}
281	
282	function test(re: RegExp, text: string): boolean {
283	  re.lastIndex = 0;
284	  return re.test(text);
285	}
286	
287	function firstMatch(re: RegExp, text: string): RegExpExecArray | null {
288	  re.lastIndex = 0;
289	  return re.exec(text);
290	}
291	
292	function scannable(file: ModerationInput): string | null {
293	  const lower = file.path.toLowerCase();
294	  if (SKIP_EXTENSIONS.some((ext) => lower.endsWith(ext))) return null;
295	  // Same reasoning as lib/secret-scan.ts: an inlined image or font is bytes,
296	  // not content, and base64 will happily contain any substring you like.
297	  return file.content.replace(DATA_URI_RE, "").replace(CLASS_ATTR_RE, "");
298	}
299	
300	function runHeuristics(files: ModerationInput[]): ModerationFinding[] {
301	  const findings: ModerationFinding[] = [];
302	  const perRule = new Map<string, number>();
303	  const seen = new Set<string>();
304	
305	  const add = (f: ModerationFinding) => {
306	    const key = `${f.rule}�${f.path}�${f.evidence}`;
307	    if (seen.has(key)) return;
308	    const count = perRule.get(f.rule) ?? 0;
309	    if (count >= MAX_FINDINGS_PER_RULE) return;
310	    seen.add(key);
311	    perRule.set(f.rule, count + 1);
312	    findings.push(f);
313	  };
314	
315	  for (const file of files) {
316	    const content = scannable(file);
317	    if (content === null) continue;
318	
319	    // Every password field's offset, not just the first: the "is this exfil
320	    // channel wired to the password form?" test needs all of them.
321	    const passwordFields: RegExpExecArray[] = [];
322	    PASSWORD_INPUT_RE.lastIndex = 0;
323	    let pm: RegExpExecArray | null;
324	    while ((pm = PASSWORD_INPUT_RE.exec(content)) !== null) passwordFields.push(pm);
325	    const hasPasswordInput = passwordFields.length > 0;
326	    const nearAPasswordField = (index: number) =>
327	      passwordFields.some((p) => Math.abs(p.index - index) <= SAME_FORM_RADIUS);
328	    const hasWalletConnect = test(WALLET_CONNECT_RE, content);
329	
330	    // ── Rule: brand impersonation of a credential form ──────────────────
331	    // Three legs, all required, because each one alone is common and benign:
332	    //   1. the file actually collects a password (a link to a login page or an
333	    //      OAuth button does not),
334	    //   2. a third-party brand is named,
335	    //   3. within ~160 chars of that name, the page SOLICITS credentials in the
336	    //      second person.
337	    // Plus a negative check that the brand isn't merely being linked, credited,
338	    // or offered as an identity provider.
339	    if (hasPasswordInput) {
340	      for (const { brand, re } of IMPERSONATION_TARGETS) {
341	        re.lastIndex = 0;
342	        let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
343	        while ((m = re.exec(content)) !== null) {
344	          const before = content.slice(Math.max(0, m.index - 40), m.index);
345	          if (BENIGN_BRAND_CONTEXT_RE.test(before)) continue;
346	
347	          const around = windowAround(content, m.index, m[0].length, BRAND_WINDOW_RADIUS);
348	          if (test(CREDENTIAL_SOLICITATION_RE, around)) {
349	            add({
350	              rule: "brand-impersonation-credential-form",
351	              severity: "high",
352	              path: file.path,
353	              evidence: snippet(content, m.index, m[0].length),
354	              note: `A password field sits on a page that asks the visitor to sign in to / verify a ${brand} account. Publishing a login page branded as someone else's service is not allowed.`,
355	            });
356	          } else {
357	            // Recorded, never blocking: a third-party brand next to a login
358	            // form is usually an integration list, a partner logo, or an OAuth
359	            // provider. Worth having in the record if the site is reported.
360	            add({
361	              rule: "brand-mention-near-credential-form",
362	              severity: "low",
363	              path: file.path,
364	              evidence: snippet(content, m.index, m[0].length),
365	              note: `${brand} is named in a file that also contains a password field. Usually benign (integration, partner, or OAuth button) — recorded for context only.`,
366	            });
367	          }
368	        }
369	      }
370	    }
371	
372	    // ── Rule: credentials leaving via a known drop channel ───────────────
373	    if (hasPasswordInput) {
374	      for (const { name, re, nearPassword } of EXFIL_CHANNELS) {
375	        re.lastIndex = 0;
376	        let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
377	        while ((m = re.exec(content)) !== null) {
378	          // Not `continue`-on-first-miss: a site can use formsubmit.co twice,
379	          // once for a harmless contact form and once for the password form.
380	          if (nearPassword && !nearAPasswordField(m.index)) continue;
381	          add({
382	            rule: "credential-exfil-channel",
383	            severity: "high",
384	            path: file.path,
385	            evidence: snippet(content, m.index, m[0].length),
386	            note: `A password field is submitted to a ${name}. That is a credential drop site, not a form backend.`,
387	          });
388	          break;
389	        }
390	      }
391	
392	      // ── Rule: credentials POSTed off-origin ────────────────────────────
393	      // Medium, not high: a real product's login page legitimately posts to its
394	      // own API on another host. We can't tell that apart from a drop site
395	      // without knowing the site's intended origin, so this records rather than
396	      // blocks.
397	      OFF_ORIGIN_POST_RE.lastIndex = 0;
398	      let om: RegExpExecArray | null;
399	      while ((om = OFF_ORIGIN_POST_RE.exec(content)) !== null) {
400	        add({
401	          rule: "credential-post-off-origin",
402	          severity: "medium",
403	          path: file.path,
404	          evidence: snippet(content, om.index, om[0].length),
405	          note: `A file containing a password field submits to an off-origin URL (${om[1].slice(0, 80)}). Legitimate if that is your own backend.`,
406	        });
407	      }
408	
409	      // ── Rule: a password field at all ─────────────────────────────────
410	      // Informational. Published projects are static builds with no server, so
411	      // a password box here can never actually authenticate anyone — but mock
412	      // login UIs and design demos are a real, legitimate thing people build.
413	      add({
414	        rule: "password-form-on-static-site",
415	        severity: "low",
416	        path: file.path,
417	        evidence: snippet(content, passwordFields[0].index, passwordFields[0][0].length),
418	        note: "Password input on a statically hosted site (no backend). Recorded for context only.",
419	      });
420	    }
421	
422	    // ── Rule: seed-phrase / private-key capture ─────────────────────────
423	    // A wallet's recovery phrase has exactly one legitimate destination: the
424	    // wallet. Any web form asking for one is a drainer. The only real
425	    // ambiguity is educational copy warning people NOT to enter it, which is
426	    // why the warning check exists.
427	    SEED_PHRASE_RE.lastIndex = 0;
428	    let sm: RegExpExecArray | null;
429	    while ((sm = SEED_PHRASE_RE.exec(content)) !== null) {
430	      const around = windowAround(content, sm.index, sm[0].length, INPUT_WINDOW_RADIUS);
431	      if (!test(INPUT_ELEMENT_RE, around)) continue; // prose about seed phrases, no form
432	      const isWarning = SEED_WARNING_RE.test(around);
433	      add({
434	        rule: "wallet-seed-phrase-capture",
435	        severity: isWarning ? "low" : "high",
436	        path: file.path,
437	        evidence: snippet(content, sm.index, sm[0].length),
438	        note: isWarning
439	          ? "Seed-phrase wording near an input, but the surrounding copy reads as a warning not to share one. Recorded, not blocking."
440	          : "An input field asks for a wallet seed / recovery phrase or private key. No legitimate site collects these.",
441	      });
442	    }
443	
444	    // ── Rule: wallet-connect + asset-delegation primitive ───────────────
445	    if (hasWalletConnect) {
446	      let matchedPrimitive = false;
447	      for (const { name, re } of DRAINER_PRIMITIVES) {
448	        const m = firstMatch(re, content);
449	        if (!m) continue;
450	        matchedPrimitive = true;
451	        add({
452	          rule: "wallet-drainer-approval",
453	          severity: "high",
454	          path: file.path,
455	          evidence: snippet(content, m.index, m[0].length),
456	          note: `Page connects a wallet and then requests ${name} — permission to move assets it does not own. That is the shape of a drainer, not a payment.`,
457	        });
458	      }
459	      if (!matchedPrimitive) {
460	        const m = firstMatch(WALLET_CONNECT_RE, content);
461	        if (m) {
462	          add({
463	            rule: "wallet-connect-present",
464	            severity: "low",
465	            path: file.path,
466	            evidence: snippet(content, m.index, m[0].length),
467	            note: "Page connects a browser wallet. Unusual for a generated static site (the build foundation ships no web3 dependencies) but not abusive on its own.",
468	          });
469	        }
470	      }
471	    }
472	
473	    // ── Rule: runtime-decoded executable payload ────────────────────────
474	    {
475	      const m = firstMatch(OBFUSCATED_PAYLOAD_RE, content);
476	      if (m) {
477	        add({
478	          rule: "runtime-obfuscated-payload",
479	          severity: "medium",
480	          path: file.path,
481	          evidence: snippet(content, m.index, m[0].length),
482	          note: "Code decodes a string and executes it at runtime. Minifiers do not emit this shape; it is normally used to hide a destination URL.",
483	        });
484	      }
485	    }
486	  }
487	
488	  return findings;
489	}
490	
491	/**
492	 * The current analyzer: pattern conjunctions over file text. Cheap, synchronous
493	 * in practice, and honest about its ceiling (see the header comment).
494	 */
495	export const heuristicProvider: ModerationProvider = {
496	  name: "heuristics-v1",
497	  analyze: async (files) => runHeuristics(files),
498	};
499	
500	let activeProvider: ModerationProvider = heuristicProvider;
501	
502	/**
503	 * Swap in a different analyzer — a model call, a vendor API, a shadow-mode
504	 * ensemble. Callers of moderateForPublish() do not change. Intended for tests
505	 * and for the eventual real classifier; there is no runtime config for it yet.
506	 */
507	export function setModerationProvider(provider: ModerationProvider): void {
508	  activeProvider = provider;
509	}
510	
511	/**
512	 * Analyzes the files about to become publicly reachable and returns what it
513	 * found. Returns findings, NOT a verdict — the caller applies policy (today:
514	 * app/api/projects/[id]/publish/route.ts refuses on `high`, records the rest).
515	 *
516	 * Async on purpose even though the current provider is pure CPU: a real
517	 * classifier will be a network call, and this signature is the seam.
518	 */
519	export async function moderateForPublish(files: ModerationInput[]): Promise<ModerationResult> {
520	  const findings = await activeProvider.analyze(files);
521	  return { provider: activeProvider.name, findings };
522	}

I read every file in scope plus the callers needed to judge them. Findings below, ordered by severity, with SAFE verdicts stated explicitly where they apply.

## 1. Prisma raw queries — ALL SAFE

Only `lib/retention.ts` has raw SQL in the review scope. Every one is a parameterized tagged template; there is no `$queryRawUnsafe` / `$executeRawUnsafe` anywhere in the repo (I grepped the whole tree, excluding `node_modules`).

- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\retention.ts:174-175` — `SELECT pg_total_relation_size(${`"${table}"`}::regclass) AS size`. The nested template builds the *value* `"Session"` and hands it to Prisma as a bind parameter, not as SQL text. Even so it can only ever be a constant: `relationBytes()` is private and reached only via `estimateBytes()`, called at `:230` (`"Session"`), `:328` (`"Event"`), `:354` (`"StripeEvent"`) — all string literals. SAFE.
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\retention.ts:264-278` — `Prisma.sql` fragment with `${SNAPSHOT_KEEP_PER_PROJECT}` and `${cutoff}`; both bind as parameters and both are module constants / a `Date`. Composed into `$queryRaw` at `:286-289` and `:301-305`. SAFE.
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\retention.ts:305` — `LIMIT ${take}`, where `take` is `BATCH_SIZE` (500) from `purgeInBatches`. Parameterized. SAFE.

## 2. Hardcoded credentials — NONE FOUND

No secret literals in any file in scope. Every credential is read from the environment:
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\mail.ts:15-18` — SMTP host/port/user/pass all from `process.env`.
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\enhance.ts:65` — `apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
The only literals present are non-secret defaults: a from-address and a contact address at `lib/mail.ts:23-24`, and a foundation path at `scripts/install-foundation.mjs:8`. `.env*` is gitignored.

## 3. Secrets in logs / responses

- **SAFE, and deliberately so:** `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\scripts\retention.mjs:86-94`. `describeDatabase()` parses `DATABASE_URL` and prints only `url.host + url.pathname`, with the comment `/** Host + database only. The connection string carries a password. */`. The password never reaches stdout. Good pattern.
- **Low:** `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\events.ts:70-73` — `console.error(\`[events] failed to record ${name}:\`, err)` dumps a raw Prisma error. Prisma errors can echo back the offending `data` payload. Per the module's own contract at `lib/events.ts:13-14` props are ids/counts/enums only, so this is bounded — but it is an unfiltered error object in logs, and it is the one place a props-discipline regression would leak into log storage.
- **PII, not a secret:** `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\scripts\promote-admin.mjs:42` prints every admin's email address to stdout on every run, including on a no-op. If this is ever run in CI or a recorded shell session, the full admin roster lands in the log.
- No secret is returned in any HTTP response from the files in scope.

## 4. Zip-slip in `lib/zip.ts` — SAFE, with one cosmetic residual

`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\zip.ts:61-67`:
```
    .replace(/\\/g, "/")
    .split("/")
    .filter((segment) => segment !== "" && segment !== "." && segment !== "..")
```
This normalizes backslashes first (so `..\..\x` is caught), then drops empty segments (kills leading `/` → absolute paths, and collapses `//`), `.`, and `..`. Traversal is not merely rejected but stripped, and `lib/zip.ts:91` skips any entry whose sanitized name is empty. There is no unzip path in this codebase at all, so the only exposure is the user's own extractor.

Defense in depth is genuine here: entry paths come from `ProjectFile.path`, which the agent can only write through `normalizePath` at `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\agent.ts:164-170` (rejects `..`, leading `/`, backslashes, and anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`).

Residual, minor: a Windows drive prefix survives sanitization — `C:\Windows\x` becomes the entry name `C:/Windows/x`. Practically unreachable (the `normalizePath` charset bans `:`), and mainstream extractors treat it as relative, but the filter is segment-based and has no drive-letter case.

Related and SAFE: `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\api\projects\[id]\export\route.ts:42` re-sanitizes the slug before it goes into `Content-Disposition` at `:55`, blocking response-header/filename injection; `:22-24` scopes the project lookup by `userId` in the same query as `id`, so cross-tenant export returns an indistinguishable 404.

## 5. Command execution

Two call sites, both `execFileSync` (argv array, no shell string), neither with user-controlled arguments.

- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\scripts\install-foundation.mjs:37-41` — `execFileSync(isWindows ? "npm.cmd" : "npm", ["install"], { cwd: FOUNDATION_DIR, shell: isWindows })`. `shell: true` on Windows only, and the comment at `:33-35` correctly justifies it (CVE-2024-27980 `.cmd` spawn). Both the binary name and the arg are literals. The one thing operator-controlled is `cwd`, from `KODELY_FOUNDATION_DIR` (`:8`) — that is an env var, not user input, but note that `npm install` in an attacker-writable `FOUNDATION_DIR` would execute that directory's `package.json` lifecycle scripts. It writes its own `package.json` first (`:30`) so the dependency set is fixed; the risk is only in the directory itself. SAFE as written.
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\scripts\eval\run.mjs:116` — `execFileSync("git", args, ...)` with constant arg arrays (`rev-parse`, `status`). SAFE.
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\enhance.ts:143-157` spawns a Claude Code process via the SDK. Worth noting as *correct*: `allowedTools: []`, `settingSources: []`, `cwd: tmpdir()`, `maxTurns: 1`. The user prompt is data, not argv, and the agent has no tool with which to touch the repo. The comment at `:132-137` also documents that importing `./agent-sdk` strips `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the child environment.

## 6. Scripts that write to the DB without authentication

All of these authenticate by shell access only — that is the design, and `promote-admin.mjs:1-8` argues the case correctly (a self-serve HTTP promote endpoint would be privilege escalation). The risk is what happens when one is run against prod.

**`promote-admin.mjs` — how it chooses who to promote.** `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\scripts\promote-admin.mjs:11` takes `process.argv[2]`, trims and lowercases it, then `:21` does an exact `findUnique({ where: { email } })` and `:31` sets `role: "ADMIN"`. So: exact email match, one argument, no pattern matching, no fallback to "first user", no bulk path. That part is sound. What is missing:
- **No confirmation and no dry-run.** Contrast `scripts/retention.mjs:36` and `:155-159`, where deletion requires an explicit `--apply` and dry-run is the default. Granting ADMIN — which per `:35-36` means access to cost, margin and customer prompts — is a one-shot, unprompted, irreversible-in-practice write with no `--yes` gate.
- **No environment guard.** `:7-8` acknowledges the hazard in a comment ("Run it against the database you mean") but nothing enforces it. Unlike `scripts/retention.mjs:60-68` and `scripts/seo/seed.mjs:39-43`, this script never calls `loadEnv` and never prints which database it hit, so the operator gets no confirmation of target before or after the write.
- **No audit trail.** The role change is not written to `Event` (no `track()` call), so a prod promotion leaves no record anywhere except the operator's terminal.
- A typo'd email is a safe no-op (`:22-25` exits), which is good.

**`insert-seo-batch{1,2,3,4}.mjs` — the sharpest edge in `scripts/`.** `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\scripts\insert-seo-batch1.mjs:8-25` (and the three near-identical siblings, which differ only in the input filename) unconditionally upsert `bodyHtml` into `BlogPost`. That column is rendered raw at `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\blog\[slug]\page.tsx:118`:
```
<div className="article-body mt-10" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: post.bodyHtml }} />
```
These four scripts perform **no validation whatsoever** — no dry-run, no diff, no tag allow-list. The maintained pipeline (`scripts/seo/seed.mjs:51-60`) refuses to write unless `validateAll` passes, and `scripts/seo/validate.mjs:31-48,64-73` enforces a tag allow-list and explicitly rejects `src=`, `style=`, `on*=` handlers and absolute URLs. The `insert-seo-batch*` scripts bypass all of it. Anything in `seo-batchN.json` — including `<script>` or an `onerror=` handler — goes straight to a live, unsanitized public page. Compounding it, `:5` reads `./seo-batchN.json` relative to the **current working directory**, not the repo root (contrast `scripts/seo/lib.mjs:14-15`, which anchors to `REPO_ROOT`), so which JSON file gets ingested depends on where the operator happened to be standing. These four look like superseded one-offs; they are the stored-XSS path into the marketing site.

**Other scripts:** `scripts/seo/seed.mjs` is well-built — validates first (`:51-60`), `--dry-run` supported (`:27`), no delete path at all (`:16-19`), `create` rather than `upsert` on the new-row branch so a concurrent write surfaces instead of being clobbered (`:122-125`). `scripts/eval/run.mjs` never touches the DB and the loader enforces it (`scripts/eval/loader.mjs:142-148` documents that `lib/db.ts`, `lib/credits.ts` and `lib/events.ts` are deliberately never imported because they instantiate Prisma at module scope). `scripts/retention.mjs` is the model for the rest: dry-run default, `--apply` required, unknown flags rejected (`:45-54`), target database printed with the password stripped.

One low-severity note: `scripts/eval/results/` is **not** in `.gitignore` and already contains `2026-08-21T17-44-48-482Z-verify.json`. With `--save-sources` (`scripts/eval/run.mjs:262`) those files embed full generated source. Contents today are fixture-derived, not customer data, so this is housekeeping rather than a leak.

## 7. Retention windows

**StripeEvent — 365 days.** `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\retention.ts:100`: `export const STRIPE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365;`

The webhook replay analysis at `:88-99` is accurate and unusually honest. The dedupe mechanism is a row-per-`event.id` inserted *before* credits are granted, relying on a P2002 unique conflict. Stripe's automatic retries exhaust within ~3 days, so 365 days is a ~100x margin against the automated case. The residual risk is stated in the source rather than hidden: a **manual** resend from the Stripe dashboard of an event older than one year would no longer be deduped and could double-grant credits. That is a deliberate, documented trade with a human mitigation. I'd call this correctly reasoned — the replay window is effectively closed for every realistic attack, and the remaining hole requires dashboard access, which is already a trusted position.

**Session — 0 days grace.** `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\retention.ts:36`: `export const SESSION_GRACE_DAYS = 0;`

Purged the moment `expiresAt < now`, with no grace period. The rationale at `:29-35` is the right one: `lib/auth.ts` already treats an expired row as signed-out at read time, so the row has no function and its only remaining property is breach exposure. Note this is *expiry-based*, not age-based — the actual lifetime of a session is `SESSION_DAYS = 30` in `lib/auth.ts`, referenced in the rule's `threshold` string at `:382`. Nothing is deleted while still valid.

Also in scope and worth recording: `EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS = 400` (`:85`), and `NEVER_PRUNED` at `:425-459` correctly exempts `CreditLedger` as an auditable financial record from which balances are derived.

## Two smaller SAFE verdicts worth stating

- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\mail.ts:50-52` — `headerSafe()` strips CR/LF and length-caps before any user value reaches `replyTo` (`:70`) or `subject` (`:71`). This closes SMTP header injection / open-relay via the contact form; the comment at `:46-49` names the exact attack. Correct: the body at `:72` is not stripped, and does not need to be. The one thing it does not do is validate that `email` is an address at all, so a garbage `replyTo` is possible — a deliverability annoyance, not a security issue, since CR/LF are already gone.
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\lib\assets\materialize.ts:66` — `a.id.split(":").slice(1).join("-").replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, "-") || "asset"` sanitizes the asset id before it becomes a real filename under `workDir`. Dots survive the filter, but `path.join(root, kind, leaf + ".txt")` with no `/` or `\` in `leaf` means `..` cannot climb — a leaf of `..` yields the file `...txt`. SAFE. Input is the internal catalogue, not user data, either way.

**Summary of what I'd actually action:** the `insert-seo-batch*.mjs` scripts (unvalidated HTML into a `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sink, CWD-relative input) are the one genuine vulnerability. `promote-admin.mjs` needs a `--yes` gate, a printed target database, and an audit event. Everything else in scope is either safe or a documented, reasoned trade-off.
